isc2.cc.d1.risk-lifecycle: Identify the asset, the threats to it, and the vulnerabilities they could exploit
Assess likelihood x impact and rank it against the other risks
Choose a treatment: mitigate, transfer, avoid or accept
Implement the chosen treatment and verify it
Document the residual risk and have it formally accepted

items_under_review.item: Requiring each engineer to sign their change requests with a private key that only they hold
items_under_review.reason: Digital signature with a key held solely by the signer is the textbook CC example of non-repudiation; the slight pull toward Authentication (proving who submitted) is outweighed by the signed-artifact framing, and the payment-signing item makes the pattern consistent.

items_under_review.item: You report a peer who is selling leaked ISC2 exam questions to candidates
items_under_review.your_answer: Canon IV — advance and protect the profession
items_under_review.reason: Protecting the integrity of the certification and acting against a colleague who degrades it is the classic Canon IV scenario; Canon II is a weaker pull because the dishonesty is the peer's, not yours.

items_under_review.item: You tell a client up front that a specialised cloud engagement is beyond what you are qualified to deliver
items_under_review.your_answer: Canon III — provide diligent and competent service to principals
items_under_review.reason: ISC2's Canon III guidance explicitly covers rendering only services you are competent and qualified for, so III is defensible and expected, though the phrase 'tell ... up front' leans on candor and could draw a less-prepared candidate to Canon II (the prompt note and hint 1 mitigate this).
items_under_review.suggested_fix: Optional tightening: 'You decline a specialised cloud engagement for a client because it is beyond what you are qualified to deliver' — keeps the competence focus and drops the candor cue.

items_under_review.item: Implement the chosen treatment and verify it
items_under_review.your_answer: Position 4 (after choosing a treatment, before documenting/accepting residual risk)
items_under_review.reason: Treatment must be implemented and verified before residual risk can be honestly characterized and accepted; the only alternative reading (management signs off residual risk at decision time, before implementation) is a minority view at CC level.

hints.reason: The 'verify before acting' vs 'evidence checkable later' split cleanly separates the fingerprint/MFA items from both signing items.
Correctly separates organisational identity/accountability needs from individual data control; does not misdirect any item.
The 'would you owe this if nobody hired you' test routes competence and conflict-of-interest to III and the rest correctly to I/II/IV; the sales-pitch item to a prospect still lands in II.
Directly resolves the honesty-vs-client pull on the competence item toward III and does not push the sales-pitch or unauthorised-scan items out of II.
Points to identification preceding assessment/ranking; accurate.
Correctly places residual-risk documentation after implementation; somewhat telegraphs the last position but does not mislead.
